source_title: Russian drone strike on Ukrainian train platform kills 14
source_excerpt:
The strike has so far killed 14 people, with at least another 14 confirmed wounded. ( Reuters )
A Russian drone strike has killed at least 14 people on a train platform in Ukraine.
The strike comes as the occupied city of Oleshky enters the third day of a fragile ceasefire.
Kyiv has slammed the 'horrific' attack as Russia and Ukraine prepare to meet next month with US envoys in an effort to restart diplomatic talks.
A Russian drone has slammed into a busy platform at a railway station in Ukraine's Dnipro killing at least 14 people in what President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called a "horrific" attack that demands a response from Kyiv's allies.
The strike came as Ukraine and Russia strive to uphold a fragile local ceasefire in the ravaged city of Oleshky -- under Russian occupation since 2022 and where residents have faced months of food, water and medicine shortages.
The truce was holding into its third day, both countries said, with the Ukrainian human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets announcing that he had "set out with the Ukrainian delegation towards Oleshky" through Belarus and Russia.
But elsewhere, Moscow continued to pummel Ukraine.
Images released by Ukrainian emergency services showed bodies scattered across the platform. ( Reuters )
The strike at the Dnipro train station hit a platform "where a regular commuter train and a regular passenger train were standing", Mr Zelenskyy said.
By early afternoon, Dnipropetrovsk regional governor Oleksandr Ganzha said the death toll from the strike had risen to 14.
Another 14 had been wounded, he said, adding that six of them were in severe condition after suffering "multiple shrapnel wounds", including an 11-year-old boy and a man who had "both legs amputated".
Mr Zelenskyy slammed the attack as "horrific" and insisted that "sanctions against Moscow and its war machine must not be eased for as long as this Russian war continues".
Images released by Ukrainian emergency services showed bodies on the platform, rescuers helping victims to safety and two burnt-out passenger trains with their windows shattered.
French President Emmanuel Macron reacted with outrage to the attack, stressing the need for "far more than a localised ceasefire" like the one in Oleshky.
Russia has fired drones on trains across Ukraine since the first days of its 2022 invasion -- destroying hundreds of locomotives and killing several railway workers.
Ukraine's air force said it had intercepted three jet-powered drones in a daytime attack, but that a fourth evaded its defences and hit the station.
In the aftermath of the attack, Mr Zelenskyy refreshed his criticism of a deal struck this month between US President Donald Trump and his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin to ease some sanctions on Russia allowing Moscow to release diesel onto global markets.
"How many such terrorist strikes has Russia carried out against our people since sanctions were lifted on some Russian oligarchs and the energy sector, instead of de-escalating," he asked.
At least six others were killed across Ukraine in separate Russian attacks, according to local officials.
Another Russian strike on the city of Chernihiv killed two teenaged girls. ( Reuters )
A strike on the city centre of Chernigiv, north of Kyiv, killed two 15-year-old girls and wounded nearly two dozen others, including four children, the head of the city's military administration, Dmytro Bryzhynsky, said.
A drone also slammed into a multi-storey residential building in the central city of Kremenchuk, killing three and wounding several -- including a six-year-old -- the local governor said.
Russia has intensified drone and missile attacks on Ukraine in recent weeks, hitting energy sites around major cities in what Kyiv says is a bid to plunge the country into cold and darkness throughout the winter.
The Kremlin earlier this week vowed not to let up in the overall pace of the war even as the sides prepare to restart stalled talks under US mediation.
Russia and Ukraine are to meet next month with US envoys to discuss ways to end Europe's worst conflict since World War II, with no firm dates set for the talks yet.
Several previous rounds have failed to move the sides closer to a deal.
Russia demands more territory in eastern Ukraine and sweeping military and political restrictions on Kyiv.
Ukraine and its allies say ceding ground to Moscow would be tantamount to a capitulation and leave Kyiv vulnerable to future Russian attacks.
